blocks.text: These are the names of the unclean birds, both those that are read in Scripture and those that the masters of the Jews put forward from tradition. To draw up a list of them was easy for Maimonides; but he did not even attempt what we expected from such a teacher, to interpret them. And, what is more surprising, the Talmudic doctors, who are so many centuries older, explain only a few, and those very ambiguously, so that they plainly grope in sheer darkness. The Greek translators too, who lived as long before most of the Talmudists as these did before Maimonides, often got stuck here, as is shown by how little they agree with themselves and by how they pull the name of a single bird into such different meanings. In the Babylonian captivity, of course, the Jews partly forgot their own language, and the purity of Hebrew degenerated into Syriac. Hence, after the return from that captivity, the true meaning of some words that were rarely used was lost. Among these were certain names of birds. Hence Aben Ezra on Levit. XI, 29. 30., where Moses forbids eight kinds of creeping things, says: גם אלה השמנה לא נוכל לדעתם גם העופות כי אם מדברי קבלה, We cannot truly know either these eight (creeping things) or the birds, except from the words of tradition. But this tradition is nowhere extant. And the Talmudists, the authors of the traditions, refer us elsewhere, namely to skilled fowlers. Thus in [III, 122] Cholin fol. 63. b.: א״ר יצחק עוף טהור יאכל במסורת נאמן הצייד לומר עוף זה טהור מסר לי רבי א״ר יוחנן והוא שבקי בהן ובשמותיהן, R. Isaac said: A clean bird is eaten on the tradition of a trustworthy fowler, so that you may say: This bird is clean, as my master (a fowler) handed down to me. R. Iochanan: Provided he is experienced in them and in their names. Hence Maimonides, in the place cited above, section 15: כל מי שהוא בקי במינין אלו ובשמותיהן הז״ אוכל כל עוף שאינו מהם ואינו צריך בריקה ועוף טהור נאכל במסורת והוא שיהיה דבר פשוט באותו מקום שזה [col. 355] עוף טהור ונאמן צייד לומר עוף זה התיר לי רבי הצייד והוא שיוחזק אותו צייד שהוא בקי במינין אלו ובשמותיהן Whoever is practised in those species (which are forbidden) and in their names freely eats all the birds that are not in that list, and needs no further investigation. And a clean bird is eaten on the basis of tradition, when this is clearly stated in the place where the clean bird is found; and there a fowler is trustworthy, so that (the one who eats) may say: My master the fowler permitted this bird to me. That is, provided the fowler is established as practised in them and in their names. But since fowlers of this kind are nowhere to be found, he adds in section 16: מי שאינו מכירן ואינו יודע שמותיהן בודק בסימנין אלו שנתנו חכמים כל עוף שהוא דורס ואוכל בידוע שהוא מאלו המינין וטמא ושאינו דורס ואוכל אם יש בו אחד משלשה סימנין אלו הז״ עוף טהור ואלו הן אצבע יתירה או זקף והיא המוראה או שהיה קרקבנו נקלף ביד Whoever does not know those birds and does not know their names distinguishes them by these signs, which the sages have handed down to us. Every bird that tears its prey by trampling on it and devours it is plainly of those species and is held unclean. But a bird that is not rapacious and carnivorous is held clean if one of these three signs is found in it. Namely, 1. if it has a superfluous toe (that is, a spur, such as cocks have); 2. or a crop, which in Hebrew is called murea; 3. or if its gizzard can be stripped by hand (without a knife). These are taken partly from the Talmudic tractate Cholin, partly from the Chaldee paraphrase of Jonathan, which reads thus at Levit. XI, 13.: וית אלין מיניא תשקצון מן עופא דלית להון ציבעא יתירא ודלית זקפתא ודקורקבניה ליתוהי מקליף, And these species of birds you shall abhor: those which have no superfluous toe, and which have no crop, and whose gizzard is not stripped. This last I do not quite understand. Yet the Geonim make so much of this last sign that, if this one alone is lacking in a bird, they never permit it to be eaten, as Maimonides explains at length. But whoever is curious about trifles of this kind should consult the cooks of the Jews.
